seo.title: Masseria San Domenico: Thalasso Puglia Honeymoon (2026)
seo.description: Original thalassotherapy masseria on the Adriatic. Score 85/100, from $600/night. Verdict, suite pick, 7-night itinerary.

content.verdict: Masseria San Domenico is the original luxury masseria in Puglia — the property that, when it opened in 1996 under the Melpignano family, essentially invented the masseria-honeymoon category that Borgo Egnazia, Torre Maizza, and the newer arrivals have since refined. A 15th-century fortified masseria built originally by the Knights of Malta, sitting on a 100-acre olive estate on the Adriatic at Savelletri, with 40 rooms (smaller than Borgo Egnazia, more intimate, family-owned), an enormous saltwater pool fed directly from the sea, a private beach across the SS379 (accessed by a small underpass and shuttle), an 18-hole golf course (the same San Domenico course shared with Borgo Egnazia), and — the defining feature — the original Aqua Sea Therapy thalassotherapy spa, the first in Italy and still operating as the most credible wellness operation among the Puglian masserias, with seawater pools at four temperatures, marine algae wraps, and a full medical-grade thalasso program. The food at the Aqua restaurant is solid traditional Pugliese under chef Christian Tedeschi (no Michelin star but at-level cooking) and the beach club restaurant is excellent for grilled-fish lunches. The honeymoon move is an upper-floor Junior Suite with sea view in the original masseria, or one of the new Garden Suites with their own private outdoor space. The defining moment: thalasso pool morning, lunch at the beach club on the Adriatic, sunset on the original masseria terrace with the olive groves below. Caveats: the property is the most “mature” of the great masserias — feel and aesthetic are slightly more 1990s-Italian-luxury than the contemporary polish of Torre Maizza or Borgo Egnazia; the beach is across the road (underpass + shuttle) rather than walking-on-sand from the property; and the food is solid rather than exceptional. But for honeymooners who want the original Puglian masseria experience with a genuine thalassotherapy program and family-owned warmth that the bigger Borgo Egnazia does not replicate, San Domenico remains the choice.
content.best_room: An upper-floor Junior Suite with sea view in the original masseria — the original 15th-century stone vaulting overhead and the Adriatic in the distance. For something more contemporary and private, a Garden Suite with private outdoor terrace. Avoid the standard ground-floor rooms in the courtyard — lovely but without the view that is the whole point.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Arrival and Aqua dinner
itinerary_7_nights.description: Drive 30 minutes from Brindisi. Check-in to your Junior Suite, welcome Spumante. Aperitivo on the masseria terrace. Dinner at the Aqua restaurant.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Thalasso morning, beach afternoon
itinerary_7_nights.description: Full morning in the Aqua Sea Therapy thalasso pools. Lunch at the beach club. Afternoon on the Adriatic sand. Return for siesta and pool evening.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Itria Valley white towns
itinerary_7_nights.description: Driver-and-guide to Locorotondo, Cisternino and Alberobello (the trulli). Lunch at a Cisternino fornello. Return for spa. Dinner at the Aqua.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Lecce baroque day
itinerary_7_nights.description: Driver to Lecce (1h). Private baroque walking tour. Lunch at Bros’ (1 Michelin star). Return via Otranto. Spa evening.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Olive oil day and Polignano
itinerary_7_nights.description: Morning at a working frantoio. Lunch at Polignano a Mare. Afternoon swim at Cala Porto. Dinner at the beach club.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Slow masseria day
itinerary_7_nights.description: Long breakfast on your terrace. Cooking class with the kitchen for orecchiette. Lunch with your pasta. Afternoon massage. Final dinner at Aqua.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Slow departure
itinerary_7_nights.description: Final breakfast. Drive to Brindisi for departure.

caveats: Aesthetic is slightly 1990s-Italian-luxury — Torre Maizza is more contemporary.
Beach is across the SS379 (underpass + shuttle), not directly walking-on-sand.
Food is solid but not Michelin-aspirational — Borgo Egnazia’s Due Camini is a 5-minute drive.

faqs.question: Good for honeymooners?
faqs.answer: Excellent for couples wanting the original Puglian masseria experience with a genuine thalassotherapy spa. More intimate than Borgo Egnazia, more historic-feeling than Torre Maizza.

faqs.question: Best time to visit?
faqs.answer: May, June, September. October still good. Closed November to March.

faqs.question: Book in advance?
faqs.answer: Junior Suites with sea view 6 months for May–September. August requires 9+ months.

faqs.question: Adults-only?
faqs.answer: No — San Domenico is family-friendly with a kids’ club. Quieter than Borgo Egnazia but expect families in summer.

faqs.question: Best room type?
faqs.answer: Upper-floor Junior Suite with sea view in the original masseria. Garden Suite for the contemporary option.

faqs.question: How to get there?
faqs.answer: Brindisi (BDS) 30 minutes. Bari (BRI) 60 minutes. Hire car or hotel transfer €150 from BDS.
